plan.title: AD lesional vs control skin DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 skin samples (6 AD-lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, Salmon gene-level raw counts, 12000 genes) are analyzed to answer which genes and which hallmark pathways differ between lesional and control skin. Sample sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median: per grounded QC rule, it is kept through sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) and only removed with a stated reason, not by depth alone — DESeq2 size factors already account for depth differences. The core DE step follows the grounded procedure: minimal count pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smaller group size), DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization built into the model, explicit reference level (Control) with a named contrast (AD_lesional vs Control), Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of log2FC for reporting/ranking, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha=0.05. A secondary edgeR quasi-likelihood run provides a robustness check (intersection = high-confidence set) per the replicate-count rule. Enrichment uses fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (the organism-matched, locally staged 2026.1 human collection), with Reactome as a stated follow-up collection, redundancy collapsing, a 15-500 gene-set size window, and leading-edge reporting. The final report consolidates DE results, fit diagnostics, enrichment results and a full reproducibility record, explicitly flagging the low-depth sample's handling and the disputed ranking-metric choice (Wald statistic, stated up front).

fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic vs MSigDB Hallmark
DE + enrichment report with diagnostics and reproducibility record
